flawed_step: The claim incorrectly assumes that marginal distributions determine the dependence between X and Y.
counterexample: Let X and Y each have marginal distribution Bernoulli(1/2). One joint distribution assigns probability 1/2 to (0,0) and 1/2 to (1,1). Another assigns probability 1/2 to (0,1) and 1/2 to (1,0). Both have the same two marginals, but the joint distributions differ: in the first P(X=Y)=1, while in the second P(X=Y)=0.
assessment_summary: The same one-dimensional marginals can arise from distinct dependence structures, so they do not uniquely determine the joint distribution.
